body.x: IOPS Co., Ltd. (CEO Kim Youngwook) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will present its satellite operations expertise, including the innovative IOPS SPACE platform, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded in 2015, IOPS specializes in AI-driven end-to-end services, satellite ground station operations, development and services, satellite assembly and integration testing (AIT), and ground system integration. The company’s expertise has earned it many clients in South Korea, including prestigious institutions like the Korea Aerospace Research Institute and the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology.

IOPS offers optimized solutions across the entire satellite operational lifecycle, from early deployment to stable operation. With over a decade of experience operating satellites for various organizations, IOPS is a leader in ground station construction, pre-launch electrical and electronics testing, and comprehensive AIT services.

At CES 2025, IOPS will unveil its IOPS SPACE platform, drastically reducing the cost, manpower, and physical space required for satellite ground station operations. The platform enables satellite control in web and mobile environments, emphasizing flexibility and user convenience.

The fully in-house developed platform supports cost-efficient satellite management. Its integrated AI capabilities diagnose potential satellite anomalies early, minimizing the risk of malfunctions throughout a satellite’s mission lifecycle. By addressing these issues before they occur, IOPS SPACE helps prevent the creation of space debris, which poses significant challenges for satellite operations.

An IOPS representative highlighted the company’s extensive history: “Before our formal establishment in 2015, IOPS had already accumulated years of expertise as the exclusive operator of South Korea’s national space program since 2006. This legacy underscores our unparalleled commitment to the country’s space initiatives and our technical prowess.”

The representative added, “Our comprehensive support for every stage of space missions, from launch to final orbit, holds immense value in today’s expanding private space industry. By participating in CES, we aim to showcase our cutting-edge solutions to global satellite operators and actively pursue international partnerships.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
